example_prompt: Create a Cartflox payment link for a 15,000 XOF T-shirt to share on WhatsApp.

description.description: Detail of the product or service.

metadata.description: Accepted by the API but not stored on the link at the moment.

error_schema.description: Error body. `code` is present on transfer endpoints.

gotchas: Payment links live in production only: a test key gets 403 with code test_mode; create a test checkout session instead.
Keep id to check the link: GET /v1/payment-links/{id}/check takes the id, not the slug.
metadata is accepted but not stored on the link, so it cannot identify the order later.
The link is created active and never expires by itself; the customer's phone number is always requested on the page, for Mobile Money.
title and amount are required (400 otherwise).

Amount units are explicit only for currencies without minor units (XOF, XAF, GNF, UGX, RWF, CDF, MGA, KMF, DJF, BIF: whole numbers, 5000 = 5,000 XOF). For the other currencies (NGN, KES, GHS, USD...) the OpenAPI does not say whether amount is in major or minor units, and the guide only says amounts are integers in the smallest common unit with an XOF example: confirm with Cartflox before going live.
Rate limit: 60 links per minute per IP (429).

Errors are an HTTP 4xx/5xx status with a JSON body { "error": "<message>" }. Transfer endpoints add a machine-readable code, and so do some other refusals (code test_mode on payment links, rate_limited on webhook resends). A 401 says Missing API key or Invalid API Key.

evidence.source_reference: OpenAPI 2026-09-19, paths./v1/payment-links.post (operationId createPaymentLink) and info.description. Passages quoted from https://cartflox.com/docs/llms-full.txt (same snapshot date): "Amounts are integers in the smallest common unit of the currency: `5000` means 5,000 XOF."
